questions.question: In a hardware cache coherence system implementing the classic 4-state MESI protocol, what action must a processor core take when it performs a write to a cache line currently held in the 'Shared' (S) state?
options: Broadcast an invalidation (or upgrade) transaction to all peer caches and transition the line to the Modified (M) state
Immediately write the data through to main memory and remain in the Shared (S) state without alerting peer caches
Demote the line locally to the Invalid (I) state and issue a full cache line fetch from external memory
Transition the line silently to the Exclusive (E) state while allowing peer caches to retain their copies
Force all other processor cores to flush their pipelines and stall until the write commits to L3

questions.question: In a set-associative cache design, what is the primary hardware efficiency advantage of adopting a Tree-based Pseudo-LRU (Tree-PLRU) replacement policy compared to true Least Recently Used (LRU)?
options: It eliminates cache tag matching overhead by predicting the hit way before tag comparison
It tracks access history using only N - 1 tracking bits per set for an N-way associative cache, substantially reducing storage and logic complexity
It completely guarantees the theoretical minimum miss rate equivalent to Belady's optimal algorithm
It prevents all cache pollution caused by sequential memory streaming without requiring hardware prefetchers
It dynamically converts set-associative sets into fully associative partitions on high-conflict workloads

questions.question: In digital IC Design for Testability (DFT), what structural modification is introduced to transform a standard D flip-flop into a basic scan cell for scan-based testing?
options: A feedback XOR gate is attached to the output to generate transient signature registers
An internal charge pump is added to overdrive the clock input during test shift cycles
A 2-to-1 multiplexer is added at the data input, controlled by a scan-enable signal to choose between functional data and scan-in data
A master-slave shadow latch is placed in parallel to capture soft-error dumps during normal execution
The standard single-ended clock pin is replaced by a differential clock receiver to maximize shifting speed

questions.question: In synchronous low-power digital design, why does an Integrated Clock Gating (ICG) cell incorporate a level-sensitive latch before the gating gate (such as an AND gate) rather than using a simple combinational AND gate alone?
options: To level-shift the clock domain voltage up to the I/O pad supply rail
To halve the incoming clock frequency whenever the controlled logic block enters a low-power mode
To intentionally introduce clock skew to eliminate downstream hold-time violations
To prevent glitches and timing hazards on the enable signal from propagating and producing clipped, spurious clock pulses
To balance the rise and fall transition times across unbalanced tree distribution branches

questions.question: In sub-2nm semiconductor technology nodes, what is the primary physical and architectural motivation for implementing a Backside Power Delivery Network (BSPDN)?
options: To enable carbon nanotube field-effect transistors to replace silicon nanosheets on the wafer substrate
To eliminate the need for optical immersion lithography across all backend metal layers
To apply compressive mechanical stress to the substrate to double carrier mobility in planar transistors
To embed deep-trench DRAM capacitors directly underneath active logic to serve as zero-latency cache blocks
To decouple power distribution from signal routing, mitigating severe lower-layer interconnect congestion and reducing IR drop via thicker backside metal rails
